incomplete_items.summary: The subseed->residual mapping is deterministic on THIS environment, but there is no MANDATORY production gate guaranteeing it stays fixed across NumPy versions. numpy.random.PCG64 raw bits are stable, but Generator.normal (ziggurat transform) is NumPy distribution code that can change between versions; a future NumPy could produce a different, equally in-support residual set.
evidence: No production function validate_known_answer_vectors (or equivalent mandatory compatibility check) exists in confirmatory_v4_block_state.py / confirmatory_v4_manifest_integrity.py / preregistration_v4.py (grep: none).

The known-answers live only in confirmatory_v4_block_state_known_answers.json and test_confirmatory_v4_block_state.py; no active spec requires running them before manifest construction (manifest_spec §215 merely points to the JSON).

No BLOCKING NumPy-version freeze: config records numpy only in environment_versions (reference builder default {'numpy':'1.26.0'}); config block_state_sampler has no numpy_version_frozen; per the audit's Scheme-B, 'environment_versions records but does not block' is not a freeze.

The deep validator recomputes residual_value via BS.residual_value_from_subseed on the SAME NumPy, so it is a self-consistency check that CANNOT detect a Generator.normal transform drift (both generation and validation would drift together).
incomplete_items.minimal_fix: Adopt Scheme A OR Scheme B. Scheme A (recommended): add a pure production function (e.g. confirmatory_v4_block_state.validate_known_answer_vectors()) that recomputes the 6+ frozen vectors and asserts residual_value.float.hex() exact match; make the active protocol REQUIRE it to run (and pass) before any phase manifest is constructed or hashed, else EXPERIMENT_INVALID_MANIFEST_INTEGRITY; cover sampler version + PCG64 + normal transform + float.hex() exact. Scheme B: freeze the exact NumPy version in the active machine spec with a blocking check (mismatch -> INVALID) and still run the KAT.
